pages.text: When the river fell in daytime, flat stones appeared. By evening, they were underwater again. Mom brought laundry down to the riverbank on her head.
Mina tried a stone on their palm. Flat and just right! Mina wanted to build a tower with it.
Raju called, "Let's catch fish! You want to, too, right?" Mina nodded.
They chased fish in a pool. Splash, splash! Mina kept looking back at the stones.
Sonu said, "Now let's throw stones!" Mina nodded again.
The sun sank. River water crept upward.
Flat stones disappeared one by one. Mina stood holding one last stone.
Mom gently enclosed the stone on Mina's palm. "What did you want to do with this?" Mina looked up.
The next day, Mina spoke first. "Today, I want to build a tower."
It grew knee-high. Raju's stone stood at the bottom. Mina carefully stacked fitting stones above it. Holding the smallest, Sonu waited for the topmost turn.
